fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The writer says, "Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant." (Hebrews 7:22). The oath and the guarantee go together. The oath is what God said to Him: "The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’" (Hebrews 7:21). So the guarantee comes because of that oath.

Yes, baker. The writer says, "He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself." (Hebrews 7:27). Notice ONCE FOR ALL. The other high priests offered daily sacrifices, first for their own sins and then for the people's. Jesus doesn't need to do that.

Right, baker! The writer says, "…the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever." (Hebrews 7:28). The law appoints as high priests men who are weak. But the oath appointed the Son. That's quite a way to finish a chapter.
